![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/e00248d1dd5cb96a5e0099acf5da41913a805dbc388715f0b542aa821a95efa5.png)

The scatterplot above shows the relationship between the number of hours $x$ a group of people spend watching TV each night and the time $y$ they sleep each night. The equation of the trend line is $y=10-1.25x.$ 

Assuming this trend continues, estimate the time a person sleeps per night if they watch TV for $6$ hours.
question.worked_solution:
To predict the number of hours a person sleeps after watching TV for $6$ hours, we need to substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the trend line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =10-1.25x \\  & =10-1.25(6) \\  & =10-7.5 \\  & =2.5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, according to this model, a person watching TV for $6$ hours sleeps for approximately $2.5$ hours.

Note: The point where $x=6$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result *may* be unreliable.
